reading.body:
Six of the eight verified MCP clients are code editors or coding agents, which means MCP adoption is currently concentrated in software development workflows rather than general-purpose AI use.

Five of the eight clients are open-source, and four of those five publish their repositories publicly. That ratio matters because open-source clients lower the cost of verifying MCP behavior and building compatible servers, which accelerates the protocol's spread without requiring central coordination. The protocol originated with Anthropic's Claude client family, and the remaining adopters are independent products from publishers ranging from a one-person-scale open community to Microsoft, suggesting the standard has moved beyond a single vendor's control.

This data covers clients only, not servers, so it says nothing about what tools or data sources these clients can actually reach once connected. It also covers eight verified entries as of a single date, so the count reflects a snapshot rather than the full population of MCP-capable software. Nothing in this data connects to compute infrastructure, power, or physical build-out, because MCP is a communication protocol and its adoption does not directly constrain or consume those resources.
